questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: The dimensional formula of impulse is
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time = (MLT⁻²)(T) = MLT⁻¹.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A car starting from rest accelerates uniformly and reaches 20 m/s in 5 s. What distance does it cover in these 5 s?
questions.explanation: Uniform acceleration from rest gives s = ½at² = 50 m (equivalently average speed 10 m/s × 5 s).

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A stone is projected with speed 20 m/s at 45° to the horizontal (take g = 10 m/s²). Its maximum height is
questions.explanation: H = u²sin²θ/2g = 400 × ½ / 20 = 10 m.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A 2 kg block rests on a rough horizontal floor (μk = 0.3, g = 10 m/s²). A horizontal force of 10 N moves it. Its acceleration is
questions.explanation: Friction = 0.3 × 20 = 6 N; net force = 4 N; a = 4/2 = 2 m/s².

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: Masses 2 kg and 3 kg hang from the ends of a light string passing over a smooth light pulley. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the tension in the string.
questions.explanation: For the lighter mass T − 20 = 2a with a = 2 m/s², so T = 24 N (check with 3 kg: 30 − T = 6).

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A 20 g bullet moving at 300 m/s embeds itself in a 1.98 kg wooden block resting on a smooth surface. The speed of the block with the bullet is
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation: 0.02 × 300 = 2.0 × v, so v = 3 m/s.

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a thin uniform ring of mass M and radius R about a tangent lying in the plane of the ring is
questions.explanation: About a diameter I = ½MR²; parallel-axis theorem: ½MR² + MR² = 3/2 MR².

questions.topic: Physics: Mechanics and Properties of Matter
questions.q: A steel wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 1 mm² (Young's modulus 2 × 10¹¹ Pa) carries a load of 20 N. Find the extension.
questions.explanation: Young's modulus Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) gives ΔL = FL/AY = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m.

questions.q: If the absolute temperature of a black body is doubled, the power it radiates increases by a factor of
questions.explanation: By Stefan's law P ∝ T⁴, so doubling T gives 2⁴ = 16 times.

questions.q: 100 g of water at 80 °C is mixed with 300 g of water at 20 °C in an insulated container. Find the final temperature.
questions.explanation: With equal specific heat, T = (m₁T₁ + m₂T₂)/(m₁ + m₂) = 14000/400 = 35 °C.

questions.q: A Carnot engine works between 600 K and 300 K and absorbs 1200 J of heat from the source per cycle. The work done per cycle is
A simple pendulum of length 1 m oscillates at a place where g = π² m/s². Find its time period.
The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe is 150 Hz. The frequency of its second overtone is
questions.explanation: A closed pipe supports only odd harmonics: 150, 450, 750 Hz. The second overtone is the 5th harmonic, 750 Hz.

questions.q: A mass m attached to a spring of force constant k has time period T. The spring is cut into two equal halves and the same mass is attached to one half. The new time period is
questions.explanation: A half-length spring has force constant 2k, so T' = 2π√(m/2k) = T/√2.

questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux φ = BA is measured in weber (Wb = T m²).

questions.q: A battery of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected across a parallel combination of 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors. Find the current drawn from the battery.
questions.explanation: Total resistance in the circuit is 2 + 1 = 3 Ω, so I = 12/3 = 4 A.

questions.q: At the midpoint of the line joining the two charges of an electric dipole, the electric potential V and electric field E are
questions.explanation: Potentials of +q and −q cancel (V = 0) but the two fields point the same way and add (E ≠ 0).

questions.q: A 4 μF capacitor is charged to 100 V. Find the energy stored in it.
A charged particle moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity. If its kinetic energy is doubled, the radius of the circle becomes
questions.explanation: r = mv/qB ∝ v ∝ √(kinetic energy), so doubling KE multiplies r by √2.

questions.q: An ideal transformer has 2000 turns in the primary and 100 turns in the secondary. The primary is connected to a 220 V ac supply and the secondary to an 11 Ω resistor. Find the primary current.
keyPoints: Is = 11/11 = 1 A, and Ip = Is × Ns/Np = 0.05 A
questions.explanation: Output power 11 W equals input power, so Ip = 11/220 = 0.05 A.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of light (frequency above threshold and kept fixed) increases the
questions.explanation: Higher intensity means more photons per second and more photoelectrons, so the saturation current increases; KE max and stopping potential depend on frequency.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: Find the energy of a photon of wavelength 620 nm in eV (take hc = 1240 eV nm).
questions.explanation: E = 1240 eV nm / 620 nm = 2 eV.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from it. The image distance is

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: Using En = −13.6/n² eV for hydrogen, find the energy of the photon emitted when an electron jumps from n = 2 to n = 1.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: A radioactive sample has an activity of 800 counts/s which falls to 100 counts/s after 1 hour. Its half-life is
questions.explanation: 800 → 100 is a factor of 8 = 2³, so three half-lives in 60 min; T½ = 20 min.

questions.topic: Physics: Optics, Modern Physics and Electronics
questions.q: A full-wave rectifier is fed with a 50 Hz ac input. The frequency of the ripple in its output is
questions.explanation: A full-wave rectifier produces a pulse for each half cycle, so the output frequency is 2 × 50 = 100 Hz.

questions.q: How many molecules are present in 11 g of carbon dioxide? (Molar mass 44 g/mol, NA = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Number of moles = 0.25, so molecules = 0.25 × NA ≈ 1.5 × 10²³.

questions.q: Find the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 4 g of NaOH (molar mass 40 g/mol) in water to make 500 mL of solution.
questions.explanation: M = moles/volume in litres = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 mol/L.

questions.q: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the subshell with n = 3 and ℓ = 1 is
questions.explanation: ℓ = 1 is a p subshell with 3 orbitals, holding 6 electrons.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in Fe³⁺ (atomic number 26)?
keyPoints: Five d electrons, each in a separate orbital
questions.explanation: Removing 4s² and one 3d electron leaves 3d⁵, with five unpaired electrons by Hund's rule.

questions.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.01 M Ba(OH)₂ solution at 25 °C (log 2 = 0.30). Give the value to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Ba(OH)₂ gives two OH⁻ per formula unit; pOH = −log 0.02 = 1.7 and pH = 12.3.

questions.q: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the relation between Kp and Kc is
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn with Δn = 2 − 4 = −2.

questions.q: For PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g) at constant temperature, increasing the pressure by decreasing the volume
options: shifts equilibrium towards PCl₃ and Cl₂
has no effect on the equilibrium
questions.explanation: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles (1 against 2), so the equilibrium shifts to PCl₅; Kp depends only on temperature.

questions.q: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.0693 min⁻¹. What is its half-life?
questions.explanation: For first-order kinetics t½ = 0.693/k = 10 min.

questions.q: How much charge in coulombs is required to deposit 0.1 mol of aluminium from Al³⁺ ions? (F = 96500 C/mol)
keyPoints: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al, so 3 F per mole

questions.q: Which of the following has the highest first ionisation enthalpy?
questions.explanation: N has a half-filled stable 2p³ configuration, so its first ionisation enthalpy exceeds that of O (and of B, C).

questions.q: The hybridisation of sulphur in SF₆ is
questions.explanation: Six bond pairs and no lone pair on S give sp³d² hybridisation and an octahedral shape.

questions.q: According to VSEPR theory, the shape of XeF₄ is
questions.explanation: Xe has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (octahedral electron geometry); the lone pairs sit trans to each other, giving a square planar molecule.

questions.q: What is the bond order of the superoxide ion O₂⁻ according to molecular orbital theory?
questions.explanation: Bond order = ½(Nb − Na) = ½(10 − 7) = 1.5.

questions.q: The number of unpaired electrons in the complex ion [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is
questions.explanation: NH₃ is a strong-field ligand, so Co³⁺ (d⁶) pairs up all electrons in t₂g orbitals (low spin); the ion is diamagnetic.

questions.q: The oxidation state of chromium in K₂Cr₂O₇ is
Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺ (atomic number 25) in Bohr magnetons.
keyPoints: Mn²⁺ is d⁵ with 5 unpaired electrons

questions.q: Among the hydrogen halides, the one with the highest bond dissociation enthalpy is
questions.explanation: H–F is shortest and strongest; bond enthalpy decreases down the group from HF to HI.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃ is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbons with a methyl on C-2 (numbering from the end giving the lowest locant).

questions.q: The number of sigma (σ) and pi (π) bonds in propyne (CH₃–C≡CH) is
questions.explanation: σ bonds: 4 C–H and 2 C–C = 6; the triple bond contributes 2 π bonds.

questions.q: Propene reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide to give mainly
questions.explanation: Markovnikov's rule: H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens, so Br goes to C-2 (via the more stable secondary carbocation).

questions.q: Which reagent can be used to distinguish an aldehyde from a ketone?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent to silver (silver mirror); ketones do not. The other reagents react with both.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde is treated with concentrated NaOH. The products are
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen and undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (disproportionation) to benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.explanation: The –NO₂ group withdraws electrons and stabilises the phenoxide ion, making p-nitrophenol the strongest acid; methyl group reduces acidity.

questions.q: How many structural isomers (including the straight-chain one) does pentane, C₅H₁₂, have?
questions.explanation: The alkane C₅H₁₂ has three chain isomers: pentane, isopentane and neopentane.

questions.q: Acetamide on treatment with Br₂ and NaOH (Hofmann bromamide reaction) gives
questions.explanation: The Hofmann degradation converts an amide into a primary amine with one carbon atom less: CH₃CONH₂ → CH₃NH₂.

questions.q: Which carbocation is the most stable?
questions.explanation: More alkyl groups stabilise the positive charge through inductive effect and hyperconjugation: tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl.

questions.q: Which pair correctly describes brown algae (Phaeophyceae)?
questions.explanation: Brown algae contain chlorophyll a, c and fucoxanthin, and store food as laminarin and mannitol.

questions.q: The cell wall of fungi is made mainly of
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

questions.q: In which of the following is the gametophyte the dominant, independent phase of the life cycle?
questions.explanation: In bryophytes such as Funaria the gametophyte is dominant; in pteridophytes and gymnosperms the sporophyte dominates.

questions.q: Coralloid roots associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria are found in
questions.explanation: Cycas has specialised coralloid roots that harbour N₂-fixing cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Nostoc).

questions.q: Marginal placentation is characteristic of
questions.explanation: In pea (Fabaceae) the ovary is monocarpellary and unilocular with a single marginal placenta (ovules along the ventral suture).

questions.q: Sieve cells associated with albuminous cells, instead of sieve tubes with companion cells, occur in the phloem of
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms lack sieve tubes and companion cells; their phloem has sieve cells and albuminous cells.

questions.q: Vascular bundles are closed (lack cambium) and scattered in the
questions.explanation: A monocot stem has scattered, closed vascular bundles surrounded by sclerenchymatous sheaths and no cambium.

questions.q: Annual rings in the wood of a tree appear because of
options: different activity of vascular cambium in different seasons
activity of phellogen in all seasons
fusion of primary xylem and phloem
growth of the apical meristem only
questions.explanation: Cambium forms wide-vessel early wood in spring and narrow-vessel late wood in autumn; together they make one annual ring.

questions.q: The sporophyte of a fern has 48 chromosomes in its cells. How many chromosomes will each spore contain?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so each spore is haploid with 24 chromosomes.

questions.q: In C₃ plants the Calvin cycle takes place in the
questions.explanation: The dark (biosynthetic) reactions occur in the stroma, where RuBisCO and other enzymes are located.

questions.q: In C₄ plants, the first stable product of CO₂ fixation is
questions.explanation: PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells to form the 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid.

questions.q: The net gain of ATP molecules from one glucose molecule in glycolysis is
questions.explanation: Glycolysis produces 4 ATP (substrate-level phosphorylation) but uses 2 ATP, a net gain of 2 ATP.

questions.q: How many NADH molecules are produced in one turn of the TCA (Krebs) cycle starting from one acetyl CoA?
keyPoints: Three oxidation steps reduce NAD⁺ to NADH
One FADH₂ and one GTP/ATP are also formed
questions.explanation: Per turn the cycle yields 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 GTP, and releases 2 CO₂.

questions.q: The respiratory quotient (RQ) when glucose is completely oxidised in aerobic respiration is
questions.explanation: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O: equal volumes of CO₂ released and O₂ consumed, RQ = 1.

questions.q: Elongation of internodes (bolting) in rosette plants such as cabbage is induced by
questions.explanation: Gibberellins (GA₃) cause bolting before flowering in rosette plants.

questions.q: Interveinal chlorosis in older leaves is a typical deficiency symptom of
questions.explanation: Mg is a component of chlorophyll and is mobile; its deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis in older leaves.

questions.q: Malonate inhibits the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase because it
options: resembles the substrate succinate and competes for the active site
questions.explanation: Malonate is structurally similar to succinate and is a classic competitive inhibitor.

questions.q: A plant cell has a solute potential of −0.8 MPa and a pressure potential of +0.3 MPa. What is its water potential?
questions.explanation: Water potential is the sum of solute and pressure potentials.

questions.q: The primary endosperm nucleus in an angiosperm is
questions.explanation: It forms by fusion of one male gamete with the two polar nuclei (n + n + n = 3n).

questions.q: The exine of a pollen grain is made of
questions.explanation: Sporopollenin is one of the most resistant organic materials and gives the exine its toughness.

questions.q: A test cross of the dihybrid RrYy × rryy gives a phenotypic ratio of
questions.explanation: The dihybrid produces four gamete types in equal numbers; rryy gives only ry, so the offspring are in a 1:1:1:1 ratio.

questions.q: In a cross AaBb × AaBb with independent assortment, what fraction of the offspring will be aabb?
questions.explanation: The two genes assort independently, so (1/4)(1/4) = 1/16.

questions.q: In a double-stranded DNA molecule, adenine is 30%. The percentage of guanine is
questions.explanation: A = T = 30%, so G + C = 40% and G = C = 20% (Chargaff's rules).

questions.q: In the lac operon of E. coli, the inducer that binds the repressor and switches the operon on is
questions.explanation: Lactose (allolactose) binds the repressor protein, inactivating it so that the structural genes can be transcribed.

questions.q: Which ecological pyramid is always upright in every ecosystem?
options: all of them in a pond
questions.explanation: Energy is lost at each trophic level, so the pyramid of energy is never inverted.

questions.q: The pioneer species in primary succession on a bare rock are generally
questions.explanation: Crustose lichens secrete acids that weather the rock and form the first soil in xerarch succession.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: Water vascular system is a characteristic feature of phylum
questions.explanation: Echinoderms use the water vascular system for locomotion, capture of food and respiration.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: Cnidoblasts (stinging cells) are characteristic of phylum
questions.explanation: Cnidarians have cnidoblasts used for anchorage, defence and prey capture.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: Animals in which the body cavity is not fully lined by mesoderm, called pseudocoelom, belong to phylum
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes (roundworms such as Ascaris) are pseudocoelomates.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: A fish with placoid scales, a ventral mouth and gills without an operculum belongs to class
questions.explanation: Cartilaginous fishes (e.g. Scoliodon) have placoid scales and separate gill slits without an operculum.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: The epithelium that lines the alveoli of the lungs is
questions.explanation: A thin simple squamous epithelium allows rapid diffusion of gases in alveoli and blood vessels.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: Which type of muscle is striated, involuntary and has intercalated discs?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle fibres are branched and joined by intercalated discs that allow rapid communication.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: According to NCERT, how many chambers does the heart of a cockroach have?
keyPoints: Heart is an elongated muscular tube lying dorsally
Divided into 13 funnel-shaped chambers with ostia
questions.explanation: The cockroach heart consists of 13 chambers, and blood (haemolymph) circulates in an open system.

questions.topic: Zoology: Animal Diversity and Structural Organisation
questions.q: A male frog can be distinguished from a female by
options: vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb
questions.explanation: Male frogs have vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs; females lack them.

questions.q: Vital capacity of the lungs is equal to
questions.explanation: Vital capacity is the maximum air that can be expired after a forced inspiration: IRV + ERV + TV.

questions.q: A person has a tidal volume of 500 mL and breathes 12 times per minute. Find the volume of air breathed per minute.
questions.explanation: Respiratory minute volume = 500 mL × 12 = 6000 mL per minute.

questions.q: If the heart rate of a person is 75 beats per minute, the duration of one cardiac cycle is about
questions.explanation: 60 s / 75 beats = 0.8 s per cycle.

questions.q: A person with blood group AB has
options: antigens A and B on RBCs and no antibodies in plasma
antigen A on RBCs and anti-B antibody in plasma
questions.explanation: Group AB has both A and B antigens on RBCs and neither anti-A nor anti-B in plasma, so it is the universal recipient.

questions.q: In a healthy adult, the glomerular filtration rate is about
questions.explanation: GFR is about 125 mL/min, i.e. roughly 180 litres of filtrate per day.

questions.q: Depolarisation of a nerve fibre during an action potential is mainly due to
questions.explanation: Rapid influx of Na⁺ through voltage-gated channels reverses the membrane polarity.

questions.q: Which hormone is released from the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis)?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin and vasopressin are made in the hypothalamus and released from the neurohypophysis.

questions.q: Trypsinogen is converted into active trypsin by
questions.explanation: Enterokinase secreted by the intestinal mucosa activates trypsinogen from the pancreatic juice.

questions.q: During contraction of a skeletal muscle sarcomere, the length of which band remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: The A band is the length of the thick filaments and stays constant; the I band and H zone shorten as thin filaments slide inward.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The interstitial (Leydig) cells of the testis secrete
questions.explanation: Leydig cells lie between the seminiferous tubules and synthesise androgens.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: In humans, fertilisation normally occurs in the
options: ampullary–isthmic junction of the fallopian tube
questions.explanation: The ovum and sperm fuse at the ampullary–isthmic junction of the oviduct.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: In a typical 28-day human menstrual cycle, on which day does ovulation take place?
keyPoints: It occurs at the middle of the cycle
questions.explanation: A mid-cycle LH surge induces rupture of the Graafian follicle around day 14.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is caused by a bacterium?
questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum; the other three are viral.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of structures is analogous?
options: Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita
questions.explanation: Flippers of penguin and dolphin have similar function but different origin (analogous); the other pairs are homologous.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, the frequency of the recessive allele q is 0.3. What is the frequency of heterozygotes?
questions.explanation: Heterozygote frequency is 2pq = 0.42.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The restriction enzyme EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence
questions.explanation: EcoRI cuts DNA between G and A within the palindrome GAATTC, leaving sticky ends.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The thermostable DNA polymerase used in PCR is isolated from
questions.explanation: Taq polymerase from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus remains active at the high denaturation temperature.

questions.topic: Zoology: Reproduction, Health, Evolution and Biotechnology
questions.q: The antibodies present in colostrum, the first milk, belong mainly to the class
questions.explanation: Colostrum is rich in IgA antibodies that give passive immunity to the infant.
